samples.rationale: Pulled only the named patient's clinical summary fields (diagnosis, medication, labs, allergies, encounter, clinician) plus age, sex and ward for context, under LU-CARE. Contact, financial and name fields are left out, MRN is tokenised via PSEUDO-EXPORT, and data is held 30 days under TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE, AUDIT-LOG, ROPA and PURGE-01.

Only the named patient's clinical and encounter fields needed for a care-team summary are pulled (no contact, financial or audit data), under legitimate use LU-CARE, with the MRN pseudonymised via PSEUDO-EXPORT, TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE, AUDIT-LOG and ROPA in place, and 90-day retention with PURGE-01.

Pulled only the one patient's clinical, encounter and minimal demographic fields needed for a care-team summary, excluding contact and financial data; relies on LU-CARE with TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE, PSEUDO-EXPORT, PURGE-01, AUDIT-LOG and ROPA, and 30-day retention (under the 90-day ceiling).

samples.deletion_mechanism: PURGE-01: scheduled purge on purpose completion, audited
samples.rationale: Scope is limited to the named patient and to the clinical and administrative fields needed for a care-team summary. I left out contact and financial fields, the name and the phone number. Safeguards are TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE and PSEUDO-EXPORT, the basis is LU-CARE, and retention is 30 days, under the 90-day ceiling.

Only the named patient's clinical, encounter and admission data needed for a care-team summary are pulled under LU-CARE; financial, contact and audit fields are excluded, and the MRN is pseudonymised on export (PSEUDO-EXPORT) with TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE, AUDIT-LOG and ROPA in place.

A ward census needs only each patient's ward and last encounter time, joined on MRN. The MRN is pseudonymised on export (PSEUDO-EXPORT); name, contact, clinical and financial fields are not needed. Scope is all records because every current inpatient on every ward must be listed. Safeguards: TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE. Lawful basis LU-CARE.

A ward census needs only a patient key (MRN, tokenised via PSEUDO-EXPORT), the ward, and the latest encounter time. Names, contact details, clinical and financial data are left out for data minimisation. Basis is LU-CARE, with TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE, PURGE-01, AUDIT-LOG and ROPA in place.

A ward census needs only each in-patient's ward and last encounter time, with MRN as the join key (tokenised via PSEUDO-EXPORT). Names, contact, clinical and financial fields are not needed. Lawful basis is LU-CARE, with TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE, AUDIT-LOG and ROPA in place.

A ward census needs only each patient's MRN (tokenised via PSEUDO-EXPORT), current ward and last encounter time, so the job takes those four fields across all wards. It leaves out names, contact details, clinical and financial data. Controls are TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE, PURGE-01, AUDIT-LOG, ROPA and DPO, on lawful basis LU-CARE.

A ward census with last-seen time needs only the MRN (tokenised via PSEUDO-EXPORT), ward, and latest encounter datetime; names, contact details and clinical content are unnecessary. Processing relies on LU-CARE, with TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE, PURGE-01, AUDIT-LOG and ROPA in place.

Medication, diagnosis and allergy are the only fields needed for the medication review. The pull is limited to the named patient under LU-CARE, with no identifiers fetched. Controls cited: TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE, PSEUDO-EXPORT, PURGE-01, AUDIT-LOG, ROPA, NOTICE-REG-2026, DPO.

The medication-vs-diagnosis-and-allergy review needs only the diagnosis, medication and allergy fields, plus the MRN as the linking key. The pull is limited to this patient's records, relies on LU-CARE, and uses TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE, PSEUDO-EXPORT, PURGE-01, AUDIT-LOG and ROPA. The MRN is pseudonymised on export.

A medication review against diagnosis and allergies needs only medication, primary diagnosis and allergy, pulled for this one patient under LU-CARE. No identifiers or other modules are needed. Safeguards are TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE and PSEUDO-EXPORT, with retention of 30 days (under the 90-day ceiling) and PURGE-01 for deletion.

The medication review needs only the patient's current medication, diagnosis and allergies, pulled for that patient alone under LU-CARE. No identifiers or unrelated modules are fetched. Safeguards are TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE and PSEUDO-EXPORT, and PURGE-01 deletes the data after 30 days.

Only the medication, diagnosis and allergy fields are needed for the medication review, and the pull is limited to the named patient's records. It relies on legitimate use LU-CARE. It uses TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE, PSEUDO-EXPORT, PURGE-01, AUDIT-LOG and ROPA, with DPO accountable and a 30-day retention.

Appointment reminders need only the patient's name, phone, and scheduled date/time (MRN as the key), all permitted under patient registration (LU-REG); no clinical, financial, or other fields are taken. Identifiers stay unpseudonymised because the reminder must reach the patient, and the data is purged after 30 days (PURGE-01), within the 180-day ceiling.

Appointment reminders need only the patient's name, phone, appointment date/time and MRN as a key, all within the registration purpose's permitted categories; no clinical or financial data is taken. Legitimate use LU-REG covers registration and scheduling, and pseudonymisation is not applied because the phone number must be usable to send the reminder.

Appointment reminders need only the patient's name, phone and appointment date/time, all within the registration/scheduling purpose (LU-REG); no clinical, financial or other fields are taken. Identifiers stay unpseudonymised because the phone number is needed to deliver the reminder, and data is held 30 days (under the 180-day ceiling) then purged via PURGE-01. TLS, ENC-REST and ACL-STORE protect the data in transit and in the store.

Appointment reminders fall under the registration/scheduling purpose (LU-REG); only name, phone and appointment date/time are fetched, with no clinical, financial or other unneeded fields. Direct identifiers are not pseudonymised because the reminder must reach the patient; protection comes from TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE, and purge via PURGE-01 within 30 days.

A reminder needs only the patient's name, phone number and appointment date/time, all within the registration purpose's permitted categories; no clinical or financial data is taken. Pseudonymisation is not required by policy and would prevent contacting patients, so identifiers stay in the clear, protected by TLS, ENC-REST and ACL-STORE, under LU-REG, with a 30-day retention ceiling and PURGE-01 deletion.

Billing settlement permits only administrative, contact, direct_identifier and financial data, so I fetched only the subject's billing fields (LU-BILL). I left out clinical_ehr/primary_diagnosis because it is clinical and the policy doesn't permit it, so the diagnosis cross-check can't be done in this run. Controls cited: TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE, PSEUDO-EXPORT, PURGE-01, AUDIT-LOG, ROPA.

Billing settlement permits only administrative, contact, direct-identifier and financial data, so I pulled only the subject's invoice, amount, payer and policy fields (LU-BILL). I left out clinical_ehr/primary_diagnosis because clinical data is not permitted for this purpose, so the diagnosis cross-check can't be done in this run. Controls cited: TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE, PSEUDO-EXPORT, PURGE-01, NOTICE-REG-2026, AUDIT-LOG, ROPA, DPO.

Only the named patient's financial fields are pulled for billing settlement under LU-BILL; primary_diagnosis is clinical, which the billing policy does not permit, so the diagnosis cross-check is not performed. Controls cited: TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE, PSEUDO-EXPORT, PURGE-01, AUDIT-LOG, ROPA.

Only the subject patient's financial fields and MRN are pulled for billing settlement under LU-BILL. The diagnosis cross-check is not done because clinical data is not a permitted category for this purpose, so clinical_ehr/primary_diagnosis is excluded.

Only the subject's billing fields are pulled to reconcile the invoice with the payer, under LU-BILL. The diagnosis cross-check is not done because clinical data is not a permitted category for billing settlement.

Only registration demographic and contact fields for this one patient are fetched under LU-REG. Insurance policy number and payer name are financial data, which the registration policy does not permit, so they were left out. Cover details would need a separate billing-purpose job under LU-BILL.
